title: Midcycle Budget Accelerator: Headcount & Pricing Sensitivity Scan
body:
Purpose:
This midcycle scan is intended to give leadership a compact, actionable view of how a short-term accelerated hiring plan combined with alternate pricing levers would impact run-rate margins, monthly burn, and capacity headroom over the next 9 months. Focus is on the product lines where pricing or capacity routing changes are feasible in the near term: Hosted API (SaaS), Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem sales).

Executive summary (quick takeaways):
- Tactical hire acceleration (add 18 FTEs over 3 months concentrated in SRE + Serving Runtime) increases monthly cash burn by ~$1.05M at fully loaded comp but buys ~35% throughput headroom across Dedicated pools (important for enterprise bookings).
- Pricing sensitivity: a blended +5% list price on Hosted API endpoints increases gross margin by ~2.6ppt on base assumptions; a -7% price shock reduces gross margin by ~3.6ppt and materially increases the time-to-profit for new customer cohorts.
- Capacity tuning (ramping burst reserve policy and tighter autoscale thresholds) can reduce need for hires by ~6 FTEs while keeping latency SLOs for 90% of traffic, but increases tail latency risk for peak events.
- Recommendation: Approve a stage-gated accelerator (phase hires in two tranches tied to committed ARR and capacity utilization thresholds) and pilot a modest +3% price increase on high-frequency Hosted tiers with a 30-day opt-out test and telemetry on churn/usage.

Key assumptions (base case):
- Revenue growth: 18% QoQ for product-led Hosted API; Dedicated new bookings flat for next quarter; Private deals pipeline weighted to contract starts in Q4.
- Avg revenue per token (hosted): $0.0009/token; embeddings unit price $0.0025/embed-unit.
- Cost per token (infrastructure + amortized model ops): $0.00036/token immediate baseline; quantization and batching improvements provide up to 20% cost reduction when applied.
- Hiring: median fully-loaded comp per FTE = $145k/year (includes benefits, equity refresh estimate, and infra allocation). Hiring plan front-loads ops/infra and delaying non-essential product hires.
- Capacity mapping: 1 SRE/infra FTE reduces incident MTTR and supports +3% sustained throughput per FTE through automation and config. Serving runtime engineers provide ~5% per FTE throughput improvements via kernel and batching optimizations.

Scenario matrix (summarized):
- Base (no price change, hiring as currently planned): gross margin 39.1%, monthly burn +$0.6M for scheduled hires.
- Accelerator Hire (18 FTEs over 3 months focused on SRE + runtime): gross margin 36.8% first month of ramp -> 38.5% after optimizations; monthly incremental burn +$1.05M during ramp.
- Price +3% (hosted only): immediate revenue uplift +3% on Hosted line, churn signal assumed negligible in 30-day test; gross margin +1.6ppt.
- Price -7% shock (competitor pressure): revenue uptick simulated at +8% volume but unit margin compresses, net gross margin -3.6ppt and runway shortfall increases by 1.8 months in downside models.
- Capacity tuning + hire reduction: delay/hire-reduction of 6 FTEs if aggressive autoscale thresholds and prefix caching are enabled; cost savings offset by +0.8ppt margin risk (tail latency).

Cost math (monthly cadence, simplified):
- Incremental monthly payroll cost per new hire (average): comp/12 * 1.15 (taxes + benefits) -> average $13.9k/month per hire.
- 18 hires * $13.9k = $250k/month direct payroll in ramp months; fully-loaded with ramping hiring costs & one-time hiring overhead -> ~ $350k/month in month 1, trending to $1.05M/month incremental by month 3 when infrastructure and provisioning cadence are included.
- One-time infra provisioning and license costs (GPU reservations, bare metal, storage): estimated $420k amortized over 6 months for the accelerator scenario.

Notes: price elasticity estimates derived from observed cohort behavior over prior 9 weeks, weighted toward low-elasticity enterprise customers. Consumer/low-commitment sandbox users show higher elasticity.

P&L bridge snapshot (illustrative, quarterly):
- Base revenue (Q3): $48.2M; gross margin 39.1% -> gross profit $18.8M.
- Accelerator + price +3% (blended): revenue +2.6% => $49.5M; near-term gross margin 37.9% due to hiring ramp and infra amortization -> gross profit $18.8M (basically neutral in Q3 until hires fully onboard).
- Downside price shock -7%: revenue $45.2M; gross margin 35.5%; gross profit $16.1M.

Operational triggers and gates (recommended cadence):
1) Capacity utilization gate: if Dedicated pool sustained utilization >74% for 10 consecutive business days and top-of-funnel committed ARR >= $3.2M, commence tranche 1 hires (10 FTE).
2) Revenue trigger for tranche 2: close rate on pipeline for Private deals > 40% (qualified pipeline >= $5M ARR) -> proceed with remaining hires.
3) Price pilot: roll +3% to high-frequency Hosted tiers for 30 days with daily churn and usage telemetry. If churn delta > 1.5% or MRR loss > $85k, revert.
4) Autoscale / cache experiment: enable aggressive KV prefix caching and 20% lower batch latency thresholds for a 4-week experiment; measure tail latency (95/99p) and customer complaints. If 99p latency delta > 40ms or complaints > threshold, rollback.

Sensitivity outputs (what to watch):
- Bookings-to-revenue conversion lag for Dedicated deals (long lead times increase cash pressure during hire ramp).
- Token mix shift: more embeddings-heavy usage meaningfully changes per-unit economics and price sensitivity.
- Competitor price moves in Hosted API tiers; prepare rapid rollback playbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Hiring too fast without capacity to onboard -> low productivity, wasted spend. Mitigation: tie tranche release to quantifiable SLO improvements and onboarding throughput metrics.
- Risk: Price increase drives downstream churn on low-commitment customers. Mitigation: target experiment to high-frequency, committed customers and expose test cohorts via billing tags.
- Risk: Autoscale and cache tuning reduces margin protection for peak events. Mitigation: reserve quick-fallback policy and small burst reserve budget for 90 days.

Next steps (decision checklist):
- Approve tranche-gated hiring authority up to 18 FTEs with finance holdback of 25% until tranche gates validated.
- Approve +3% Hosted pilot for 30 days with telemetry and rollback criteria.
- Prioritize engineering experiment for aggressive KV prefix caching and autoscale thresholds (4-week sprint).
- Finance to model incremental burn impact in detailed monthly cash-flow workbook and share with CEO/GC by 2026-06-10.

Appendix A: raw sensitivity inputs (for modeling team) - quick list of numbers:
